title.zh: 第二十九 輿服上 玉輅 乘輿 金根 安車 立車 耕車 戎車 獵車 軿車 青蓋車...
title.en: Volume 119: Travel and Dress Part One
title.raw: 第二十九 輿服上 玉輅 乘輿 金根 安車 立車 耕車 戎車 獵車 軿車 青蓋車... Volume 119: Travel and Dress Part One

sentences.zh: 《書》曰：「明試以功，車服以庸。

translations.literal: The Documents says: “Clearly test them by their deeds; grant chariots and robes according to their merit.”
translations.idiomatic: The Classic of Documents declares: “Prove their worth by what they achieve, then reward merit with the carriages and vestments befitting it.”

sentences.zh: 」言昔者聖人興天下之大利，除天下之大害，躬親其事，身履其勤，憂之勞之，不避寒暑，使天下之民物，各得安其性命，無夭昏暴陵之災。

translations.literal: It means that in antiquity the sage raised the great benefits for all under Heaven and removed the great harms for all under Heaven; he personally undertook the task, himself endured the toil, worried and labored over it, did not shun cold or heat, and caused the people and creatures of the world each to secure their lives and persons without the disasters of premature death, violence, or oppression.
translations.idiomatic: The sense is this: the ancient sage labored for the common good of the realm and swept away its gravest evils—taking the burden on his own shoulders, braving every season, until every living thing could keep its natural span free from untimely death, tyranny, or plunder.

sentences.zh: 是以天下之民，敬而愛之，若親父母；

translations.literal: Therefore the people of the world revered and loved him as if he were father and mother;
translations.idiomatic: So the folk revered and cherished him as they would their own parents;

sentences.zh: 則而養之，若仰日月。

translations.literal: they took him as their model and nurtured him as if gazing up at sun and moon.
translations.idiomatic: they took his example for their nurture, as one lifts the face toward sun and moon.

sentences.zh: 夫愛之者欲其長久，不憚力役，相與起作宮室，上棟下宇，以雍覆之，欲其長久也；

translations.literal: Those who loved him desired his long endurance; they did not shrink from labor service; together they raised palaces with ridgepole above and rafters below to shelter him thickly, desiring his long endurance;
translations.idiomatic: Love made them wish him to endure forever, so they shouldered corvée without complaint and raised halls—beams aloft, eaves below—to roof him in, all so his reign might last.

sentences.zh: 敬之者欲其尊嚴，不憚勞煩，相與起作輿輪旌旗章表，以尊嚴之。

translations.literal: those who revered him desired his dignity; they did not shrink from toil and trouble; together they made chariot wheels, banners, flags, and insignia to lend him dignity.
translations.idiomatic: Reverence made them wish him awe-inspiring rank, so they forged wheels, flew standards, and forged regalia that matched his majesty.

sentences.zh: 斯愛之至，敬之極也。

translations.literal: This is the utmost of love and the extreme of reverence.
translations.idiomatic: Such was love pressed to its limit and reverence carried to its height.

sentences.zh: 苟心愛敬，雖報之至，情由未盡。

translations.literal: If in the heart there is true love and reverence, even when repayment reaches its utmost, the feeling still cannot be exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Where love and reverence are genuine, no repayment, however lavish, can ever discharge the debt of feeling.

sentences.zh: 或殺身以為之，盡其情也；

translations.literal: Some gave their bodies for it, exhausting their devotion;
translations.idiomatic: Some laid down their lives—such was the depth of their devotion;

sentences.zh: 弈世以祀之，明其功也。

translations.literal: age after age they sacrificed to him, clarifying his merit.
translations.idiomatic: generation after generation they kept his shrines lit, proclaiming his achievement to posterity.

sentences.zh: 是以流光與天地比長。

translations.literal: Therefore his flowing radiance vies in length with Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: Thus his fame runs on beside heaven and earth without end.

sentences.zh: 後世聖人，知恤民之憂思深大者，必饗其樂；

translations.literal: Later sages, knowing that those who deeply ponder the people’s cares must enjoy their pleasures;
translations.idiomatic: Later sages understood that rulers who take the people’s anxieties to heart are owed their joys in turn;

sentences.zh: 勤仁毓物使不夭折者，必受其福。

translations.literal: those who labor at benevolence and nurture things so they do not die young must receive their blessing.
translations.idiomatic: and that those who labor at humanity, cherishing life so none dies before its time, earn a blessing in return.

sentences.zh: 故為之製禮以節之，使夫上仁繼天統物，不伐其功，民物安逸，若道自然，莫知所謝。

translations.literal: Therefore they made ritual to regulate it, so that the highest benevolence, continuing Heaven’s thread and ordering things, did not boast of its achievement, and people and creatures rested at ease as if the way were spontaneous, none knowing whom to thank.
translations.idiomatic: So they framed rite and music to set bounds: the supreme humanity that carries heaven’s pattern and orders the world must never trumpet its own work; the people thrive as if by nature itself, unaware whom to praise.

sentences.zh: 《老子》曰：「聖人不仁，以百姓為芻狗」。

translations.literal: The Laozi says: “The sage is not benevolent; he treats the hundred surnames like straw dogs.”
translations.idiomatic: Laozi writes: “The sage is not ‘kind’ in the small sense; he holds the common people as ritual straw dogs—deployed without clinging.”

sentences.zh: 此之謂也。

translations.literal: This is what it refers to.
translations.idiomatic: The passage means just this.

sentences.zh: 夫禮服之興也，所以報功章德，尊仁尚賢。

translations.literal: The rise of ritual vestments is the means to repay achievement, display virtue, honor benevolence, and esteem the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Court dress and chariot regalia arose to reward merit, make virtue visible, exalt humanity, and honor the worthy.

sentences.zh: 故禮尊尊貴貴，不得相逾，所以為禮也，非其人不得服其服，所以順禮也。

translations.literal: Therefore ritual honors the honorable and esteems the estimable; they may not encroach on one another—this is how it becomes ritual; if it is not that person, he may not wear that garb—this is how ritual is obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: Rite therefore grades the high above the low and forbids trespass—that is what makes it ritual; no one may don insignia above his station—that is what makes it binding.

sentences.zh: 順則上下有序，德薄者退，德盛者縟。

translations.literal: When it is obeyed, high and low have order; the thin in virtue withdraws, the rich in virtue is ornate.
translations.idiomatic: When it is honored, superiors and inferiors fall into rank; the mean in virtue falls back, the abundant in virtue shines forth.

sentences.zh: 故聖人處乎天子之位，服玉藻邃延，日月昇龍，山車金根飾，黃屋左纛，所以副其德，章其功也。

translations.literal: Therefore the sage occupying the Son of Heaven’s place wears jade pendants and deep mian-crown with hanging threads, sun and moon and ascending dragon, mountain chariot and gold-root ornament, yellow canopy and left yak-tail banner, thereby matching his virtue and displaying his achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the true king on the throne wears the deep-crowned diadem hung with jade beads, robes figured with sun, moon, and ascending dragon, chariot fittings of the “mountain” and gold-root types, the yellow canopy and the yak-tail standard at the left—all to answer his virtue and proclaim his merit.

sentences.zh: 賢仁佐聖，封國受民，黼黻文繡，降龍路車，所以顯其仁，光其能也。

translations.literal: The worthy and benevolent who assist the sage, receiving states and people, wear axe-and-fu emblems and patterned embroidery, descending dragon and road chariot, thereby displaying their benevolence and magnifying their ability.
translations.idiomatic: Worthy helpers who receive fiefs ride chariots of state emblazoned with paired dragons, their silks brocaded with axe-and-fu motifs—insignia that broadcast their humanity and capacity.

sentences.zh: 及其季末，聖人不得其位，賢者隱伏，是以天子微弱，諸侯脅矣。

translations.literal: Reaching the late age, the sage did not obtain his place and the worthy hid; therefore the Son of Heaven grew weak and the feudal lords were coercive.
translations.idiomatic: By the final generations the sage-king had lost his seat and good men withdrew to obscurity; the throne grew feeble while regional lords threw their weight about.

sentences.zh: 於此相貴以等，相讟以貨，相賂以利，天下之禮亂矣。

translations.literal: Here they honored one another by rank, slandered one another by goods, bribed one another by profit, and the ritual of the world was in chaos.
translations.idiomatic: Then lords measured one another by title alone, traded slander for wealth, bought loyalty with gain, and the empire’s ritual order collapsed.

sentences.zh: 至週夷王下堂而迎諸侯，此天子失禮，微弱之始也。

translations.literal: Down to King Yi of Zhou descending the hall to welcome the feudal lords—this was the Son of Heaven losing ritual, the beginning of weakness.
translations.idiomatic: It began when King Yi of Zhou stepped down from his dais to greet vassal lords—a Son of Heaven already surrendering proper precedence.

sentences.zh: 自是諸侯宮縣樂食，祭以白牡，擊玉磬，朱幹設鍚，冕而儛《大武》。

translations.literal: From this the feudal lords hung graded bells and took their meals to music, sacrificed with white bull, struck jade chimes, set red shield with golden shield-boss, wore the mian-cap and danced the Great Martial.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter princes claimed royal music at their meals, offered the white bull reserved for the Son of Heaven, sounded jade lithophones, carried crimson shields bossed in gold, and performed the Great Martial dance in full regalia.

sentences.zh: 大夫臺門旅樹反坫，繡黼丹朱中衣，鏤簋朱紘，此大夫之僭諸侯禮也。

translations.literal: Grandees had gate-towers, avenue trees, and inverted stands for goblets, fu-and-axe embroidery on the inner robe, carved gui vessels and vermillion cap-strings—this was grandees usurping the ritual of feudal lords.
translations.idiomatic: Great officers raised twin gatehouses, lined their approaches with trees, set up the lordly cup-stand, wore inner robes brocaded with axe emblems, used carved sacrificial gui and crimson cap cords—every one a prerogative of a marquis.

sentences.zh: 《詩》刺「彼己之子，不稱其服」，傷其敗化。

translations.literal: The Odes satirize “those men there—they do not match their dress,” grieving that they ruin transformation.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Poetry mocks “those fellows in finery that outranks their virtue,” lamenting how counterfeit splendor corrupts the moral order.

sentences.zh: 《易》譏「負且乘，致寇至」，言小人乘君子器，盜思奪之矣。

translations.literal: The Changes ridicules “carrying on the back and riding in the carriage, bringing robbers to arrive,” meaning the petty man rides the gentleman’s vessel and thieves plot to seize it.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes warns that when a mean man mounts a noble’s carriage, bandits already plot to strip him—the vessel summons the theft.

sentences.zh: 自是禮制大亂，兵革並作；

translations.literal: From this the ritual system was greatly chaotic and arms arose together;
translations.idiomatic: Hence ritual unraveled and arms flared everywhere;

sentences.zh: 上下無法，諸侯陪臣，山楶藻梲。

translations.literal: high and low had no model; feudal lords and their retainers used mountain capitals on pillars and painted rafter-blocks.
translations.idiomatic: high and low lost all measure until even vassals and household ministers carved mountain-shaped capitals and painted their roof beams like kings.

sentences.zh: 降及戰國，奢僭益熾，削滅禮籍，蓋惡有害己之語。

translations.literal: Descending to the Warring States, extravagance and usurpation blazed hotter; they cut away the ritual canopies, probably hating words that harmed themselves.
translations.idiomatic: By the Warring States excess and trespass burned brighter still; rulers shredded the ritual codices, loathing any text that might curb their ambition.

sentences.zh: 競修奇麗之服，飾以輿馬，文罽玉纓，象鑣金鞍，以相誇上。

translations.literal: They vied to trim outlandish garments, ornamented with chariots and horses, patterned felts and jade tassels, ivory cheek-pieces and gold saddles, to outdo one another upward.
translations.idiomatic: They raced to outdo one another in bizarre silks, gilded saddlery, jade-hung bridles, and ivory-mounted harness—each display grander than the last.

sentences.zh: 爭錐刀之利，殺人若刈草然，其宗祀亦旋夷滅。

translations.literal: They fought over profit the size of an awl’s point and killed men as if mowing grass; their ancestral sacrifices were also soon extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: They slaughtered for margins slimmer than an awl-tip, reaping lives like hay, and in the same breath saw their own lineages snuffed out.

sentences.zh: 榮利在己，雖死不悔。

translations.literal: Glory and profit were in themselves; though they died they did not repent.
translations.idiomatic: So long as glory stuck to the self, they went to the grave unrepentant.

sentences.zh: 及秦並天下，攬其輿服，上選以供禦，其次以錫百官。

translations.literal: When Qin annexed the world it gathered their chariots and robes, taking the finest to supply the imperial use and the next grade to grant the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin swallowed the realm it seized every court’s carriages and costumes, reserving the best for the throne and handing the rest down the bureaucracy.

sentences.zh: 漢興，文學既缺，時亦草創，承秦之製，後稍改定，參稽《六經》，近於雅正。

translations.literal: When the Han arose, learning was still lacking and the times were also rough at the start; it inherited Qin’s system, later gradually revised it, checked it against the Six Classics, and drew near to correct elegance.
translations.idiomatic: The Han began in haste, short of classical scholars, and at first simply continued Qin usage; only by degrees did it reform the code, cross-check the Six Classics, and edge back toward proper dignity.

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：「其或繼周者，行夏之正，乘殷之輅，服週之冕，樂則《韶》、《舞》。

translations.literal: Confucius said: “Whoever may succeed the Zhou should use the Xia calendar, ride the Yin carriage, wear the Zhou cap, and for music adopt the Shao and the Wu.”
translations.idiomatic: Confucius taught that any dynasty succeeding Zhou ought to adopt the Xia calendar, the Yin-style state carriage, the Zhou ceremonial cap, and the music of Shao and Wu.

sentences.zh: 」故撰《輿服》著之於篇，以觀古今損益之義云。

translations.literal: Therefore this Treatise on Chariots and Robes is set down in the chapter to observe the meaning of ancient and modern increase and decrease.
translations.idiomatic: Hence this “Chariots and Vestments” monograph is set in writing so readers may trace how regalia has waxed and waned from antiquity to the present.

sentences.zh: 上古聖人，見轉蓬始知為輪。

translations.literal: High antiquity’s sages, seeing tumbleweed spin, first knew how to make a wheel.
translations.idiomatic: The earliest sages watched windblown pigweed roll and grasped the principle of the wheel.

sentences.zh: 輪行可載，因物知生，復為之輿。

translations.literal: The wheel could roll and carry; from the thing they knew how to produce it, and again they made the carriage body for it.
translations.idiomatic: A wheel could bear a load in motion; from that insight they learned manufacture, then framed a body to ride upon it.

sentences.zh: 輿輪相乘，流運罔極，任重致遠，天下獲其利。

translations.literal: Carriage and wheel multiplied each other, flowing and turning without limit, bearing weight and reaching distance; the world gained their benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Body and wheel worked in tandem, rolling on without end, hauling heavy freight over long roads—the world profited from the pairing.

sentences.zh: 後世聖人觀於天，視斗周旋，魁方杓曲，以攜龍、角為帝車，於是乃曲其輈，乘牛駕馬，登險赴難，週覽八極。

translations.literal: Later sages observed Heaven, watched the Dipper revolve—its ladle square, its handle curved—and took the Dragon Horn asterism as the Emperor’s chariot; then they curved the shaft, yoked oxen and drove horses, climbed peril and went through hardship, and toured the eight extremities.
translations.idiomatic: Later sages read the sky: the Dipper’s square bowl and crooked handle, the Dragon Horn stars imagined as the celestial chariot—then they curved the draught-pole, hitched ox and horse, crossed rough terrain, and ranged to the ends of the earth.

sentences.zh: 故《易·震》乘《乾》，謂之《大壯》，言器莫能有上之者也。

translations.literal: Therefore in the Changes, Thunder riding on Qian is called Great Strength, meaning no implement can surpass what is above it.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the Changes pairs Thunder atop Qian as “Great Strength”—no crafted thing may outrank what sits highest.

sentences.zh: 自是以來，世加其飾。

translations.literal: From this time onward, each age added its ornament.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward every reign layered new ornament on the design.

sentences.zh: 至奚仲為夏車正，建其斿旐，尊卑上下，各有等級。

translations.literal: Down to Xi Zhong, who for the Xia was chariot master, setting up his streamers and pennons, noble and base, high and low, each had grades.
translations.idiomatic: When Xi Zhong served the Xia as master of chariots, he standardized streamers and pennants so rank from highest to lowest matched fixed grades.

sentences.zh: 周室大備，官有六職，百工與居一焉。

translations.literal: The Zhou house was greatly complete; the offices had six crafts, and the hundred artisans occupied one of them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou perfected the system: six ministries of craft, of which chariot-making was one among many trades.

sentences.zh: 一器而群工致巧者，車最多，是故具物以時，六材皆良。

translations.literal: Of one vessel to which many artisans brought skill, the chariot had the most; therefore the parts were supplied in season and the six materials were all good.
translations.idiomatic: No single object demanded coordinated skill from so many masters as the chariot; only when every part arrived in season could the six materials meet the standard.

sentences.zh: 輿方法地，蓋圓像天；

translations.literal: The carriage box was square to image Earth; the canopy was round to image Heaven;
translations.idiomatic: The body was squared to echo earth; the canopy was domed to echo heaven;

sentences.zh: 三十輻以像日月；

translations.literal: thirty spokes to image sun and moon;
translations.idiomatic: thirty spokes stood for the days of the lunar month;

sentences.zh: 蓋弓二十八以像列星；

translations.literal: twenty-eight canopy bows to image the arrayed stars;
translations.idiomatic: twenty-eight canopy ribs mapped the lunar lodges;

sentences.zh: 龍旂九斿，七仞齊軫，以像大火；

translations.literal: the dragon banner with nine pennons, seven ren even with the end-guard, to image the Great Fire asterism;
translations.idiomatic: the dragon standard’s nine streamers, their seven-ren fall aligned with the axle guard, matched the Great Fire constellation;

sentences.zh: 鳥旟七斿，五仞齊較，以像鶉火；

translations.literal: the bird pennant with seven pennons, five ren even with the yoke-bar, to image the Quail Fire asterism;
translations.idiomatic: the bird pennant’s seven streamers, five ren level with the crossbar, answered Quail Fire;

sentences.zh: 熊旗六斿，五仞齊肩，以像參、伐；

translations.literal: the bear flag with six pennons, five ren even with the shoulder, to image Orion and the Strife stars;
translations.idiomatic: the bear ensign’s six streamers, five ren to the shoulder line, invoked Orion and Strife;

sentences.zh: 龜旐四斿，四仞齊首，以像營室；

translations.literal: the tortoise pennant with four pennons, four ren even with the pole top, to image the Encampment lodge;
translations.idiomatic: the tortoise banner’s four streamers, four ren to the crown, mirrored the Encampment lodge;

sentences.zh: 弧旌枉矢，以像弧也：此諸侯以下之所建者也。

translations.literal: the bow-banner with crooked arrows imaged the bow constellation: these were what those below the feudal lords displayed.
translations.idiomatic: the bent-arrow bow-banner echoed the Bow asterism—such were the emblems permitted below the rank of independent prince.

sentences.zh: 天子玉路，以玉為飾，鍚樊纓十有再就，建太常，十有二斿，九仞曳地，日月昇龍，像天明也。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven’s jade road chariot had jade ornament, tin cheek-pieces and crimson tassels with twelve knots, flew the Grand Constant banner with twelve pennons, nine ren trailing on the ground, sun, moon, and ascending dragon, imaging the brightness of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor’s jade-lined state carriage bore jade inlay, twelve-knot cheek tassels, and the Grand Constant standard with twelve streamers dragging nine ren on the ground, broidered with sun, moon, and ascending dragon to mirror celestial radiance.

sentences.zh: 夷王以下，周室衰弱，諸侯大路。

translations.literal: Below King Yi the Zhou house weakened and the feudal lords used the great road chariot.
translations.idiomatic: After King Yi the royal house declined, and regional lords dared to ride the great-road chariot reserved for the Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 秦並天下，閱三代之禮，或曰殷瑞山車，金根之色。

translations.literal: Qin annexed the world, reviewed the ritual of the three dynasties; some say the Yin auspicious mountain chariot, the color of gold root.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin united the realm it surveyed Three Dynasties ritual; tradition names the Yin “auspicious mountain” carriage and speaks of the gold-root hue.

sentences.zh: 漢承秦制，禦為乘輿，所謂孔子乘殷之路者也。

translations.literal: The Han inherited Qin’s system; the imperial equipage was called “riding the palanquin,” what is meant by Confucius riding the Yin road.
translations.idiomatic: Han continued Qin practice: the imperial train was termed the palanquin equipage—the carriage type Confucius had praised as “the Yin road.”

sentences.zh: 乘輿、金根、安車、立車，輪皆朱班重牙，貳轂兩轄，金薄繆龍，為輿倚較，文虎伏軾，龍首銜軛，左右吉陽筩，鸞雀立衡，B42E文畫輈，羽蓋華蚤，建大旂，十有二斿，畫日月昇龍，駕六馬，象鑣鏤鍚，金B42F方釳，插翟尾，朱兼樊纓，赤E47B易茸，金就十有二，左纛以DA3E牛尾為之，在左騑馬軛上，大如斗，是為德車。

translations.literal: The palanquin, gold root, seated carriage, and standing carriage all had wheels with vermillion flecking and double cogs, paired hubs and double linchpins, gold foil with interlaced dragons forming the body side-bars and yoke-bar uprights, patterned tigers crouching on the crossbar, dragon heads gripping the yoke, auspicious tubes left and right, luan-birds standing on the crossbeam, cloud-and-animal motifs painted on the shaft, feathered canopy with splendid finials, great banner with twelve pennons painted with sun, moon, and ascending dragon, six horses harnessed, ivory cheek-pieces with openwork tin bosses, gold shield-grip and square axle-cap, pheasant tail plumes inserted, vermillion mixed tassels on cheek and crupper, red deerskin and yak-hair ornaments, twelve gold bosses, the left yak-tail banner made from yak tail on the left trace-horse’s yoke, large as a dou measure—this is called the chariot of virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Palanquin, gold-root, seated, and standing state carriages shared scarlet-flecked double-toothed wheels, twin hubs, paired linchpins, gold-foil dragons on the side-rails, tigers on the crossbar, dragon-headed yoke, lucky tubes at either side, luan birds on the crossbeam, cloud beasts painted down the pole, plumed canopy with jeweled finials, a twelve-pennon great banner figured with sun, moon, and dragon, teams of six with ivory bits and pierced tin bosses, gold shield-mounts and square nave caps, pheasant plumes astern, vermillion cheek and crupper tassels, red hide and yak wool, twelve gold roundels, and the yak-tail standard at the left trace—large as a peck measure—the whole ensemble called the “chariot of virtue.”

sentences.zh: 五時車，安、立亦皆如之。

translations.literal: The five-seasons chariots, seated and standing, were all like this.
translations.idiomatic: The five seasonal chariots—seated and standing models—matched this specification.

sentences.zh: 各如方色，馬亦如之。

translations.literal: Each matched the color of its quarter; the horses matched likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Each matched its directional color, horses dyed or caparisoned to suit.

sentences.zh: 白馬者，朱其髦尾為朱鬣雲。

translations.literal: For white horses they vermillioned the mane and tail to make vermillion manes.
translations.idiomatic: White horses had mane and tail dyed scarlet so the team showed crimson crests.

sentences.zh: 所御駕六，餘皆駕四，後從為副車。

translations.literal: What the emperor personally drove was six-in-hand; the rest were all four-in-hand, following as secondary chariots.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign alone used six horses; all other cars ran four, trailing as escort vehicles.

sentences.zh: 耕車，其飾皆如之。

translations.literal: The ploughing chariot: its ornaments were all like these.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual ploughing carriage wore the same decorative scheme.

sentences.zh: 有三蓋。

translations.literal: It had three canopies.
translations.idiomatic: It carried a triple canopy.

sentences.zh: 一曰芝車，置𨏟耒耜之箙，上親耕所乘也。

translations.literal: One name is the lingzhi chariot; it stored hoes and ploughshares for the imperial ploughing; the emperor rode it in person when ploughing the sacred field.
translations.idiomatic: Also called the “mushroom” carriage, it stowed hoes and ploughs for the ceremonial furrow—the emperor’s personal car for the spring ploughing rite.

sentences.zh: 戎車，其飾皆如之。

translations.literal: The war chariot: its ornaments were all like these.
translations.idiomatic: The war chariot matched the same ornamental program.

sentences.zh: 蕃以矛麾金鼓羽析幢翳，𨏟冑甲弩之箙。

translations.literal: It screened spears, banners, gongs, drums, feathered splits, canopies, and shades, and stored helmets, armor, and crossbows.
translations.idiomatic: It carried spears, command flags, gongs and drums, feather screens, sun shades, and a locker for helms, mail, and crossbows.

sentences.zh: 獵車，其飾皆如之。

translations.literal: The hunt chariot: its ornaments were all like these.
translations.idiomatic: The hunting carriage used the same fittings.

sentences.zh: 重輞縵輪，繆龍繞之。

translations.literal: Double rim and wrapped wheel, with interlaced dragons winding around it.
translations.idiomatic: It had a double tire, cloth-wrapped wheel, and coiling dragon scrollwork round the felloe.

sentences.zh: 一曰闟豬車，親校獵乘之。

translations.literal: One name is the “pig-stalking” chariot; the emperor rode it when personally directing the hunt.
translations.idiomatic: Also known as the “pig-barrier” car, it carried the ruler on the imperial battue.

sentences.zh: 太皇太后、皇太后法駕，皆禦金根，加交絡帳裳。

translations.literal: The grand empress dowager and empress dowager in statutory equipage both rode the gold-root carriage, with crossed-net curtains and skirt panels added.
translations.idiomatic: On statutory progresses the two dowagers rode gold-root cars veiled with lattice curtains and hanging panels.

sentences.zh: 非法駕，則乘紫罽軿車。

translations.literal: If not statutory equipage, they rode the purple felt light carriage.
translations.idiomatic: For informal outings they used the purple felt covered gig.

sentences.zh: 雲B42E文畫輈，黃金塗五末，蓋蚤。

translations.literal: Cloud-animal motifs painted on the shaft, the five extremities gilded, canopy finials.
translations.idiomatic: The pole bore cloud-beast painting, the five metal tips were gilt, and the canopy carried jeweled finials.

sentences.zh: 左右騑，駕三馬。

translations.literal: Left and right trace horses, three horses harnessed.
translations.idiomatic: They were driven three-in-hand with traces on both sides.

sentences.zh: 長公主赤罽軿車。

translations.literal: Senior princesses used the red felt light carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Senior imperial daughters rode the crimson felt gig.

sentences.zh: 大貴人、貴人、公主、王妃、封君油畫軿車。

translations.literal: Great honored ladies, honored ladies, princesses, princes’ consorts, and titled noblewomen used lacquer-painted light carriages.
translations.idiomatic: Great and ordinary honored consorts, princesses, princes’ wives, and enfeoffed noblewomen rode lacquered, painted gigs.

sentences.zh: 大貴人加節畫輈。

translations.literal: Great honored ladies additionally had patterned painting on the shaft.
translations.idiomatic: Great honored ladies added ornamental striping to the pole.

sentences.zh: 皆右騑而已。

translations.literal: All had only the right trace horse.
translations.idiomatic: All these gigs used a single right-side trace horse.

sentences.zh: 皇太子、皇子皆安車，朱班輪，青蓋，金華蚤，黑B42E文，畫轓文輈，金塗五末。

translations.literal: The heir apparent and imperial sons all had seated carriages with vermillion-flecked wheels, green canopy, gold finials, black cloud-animal motifs, painted screen-bars and patterned shaft, the five tips gilded.
translations.idiomatic: Crown prince and princes rode seated cars with scarlet-flecked wheels, blue-green canopy, gold finials, black cloud beasts on the panels, painted sashes and pole, gilt hardware.

sentences.zh: 皇子為王，錫以乘之，故曰王青蓋車。

translations.literal: When an imperial son became a king he was granted this to ride; therefore it is called the prince’s green-canopy carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Once a prince was enfeoffed he received this model—hence the “king’s green-canopy carriage.”

sentences.zh: 皇孫則綠車以從。

translations.literal: Imperial grandsons then had green carriages following.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial grandsons followed in green carriages.

sentences.zh: 皆左右騑，駕三。

translations.literal: All had left and right traces, harnessed three.
translations.idiomatic: All used paired traces with three horses.

sentences.zh: 公、列侯安車，朱班輪，倚鹿較，伏熊軾，皁繒蓋，黑轓，右輫。

translations.literal: Dukes and full marquises had seated carriages with vermillion-flecked wheels, deer uprights on the yoke-bar, bears crouching on the crossbar, black silk canopy, black screen-bars, right-side wheel guard.
translations.idiomatic: Dukes and marquises rode seated cars with speckled red wheels, deer figures on the uprights, bears on the crossbar, black silk canopy, black sashes, and a right-side mudguard.

sentences.zh: 中二千石、二千石皆皁蓋，朱兩轓。

translations.literal: Fully two thousand piculs and two thousand piculs all had black canopies and vermillion on both screen-bars.
translations.idiomatic: Officials at full and straight two thousand piculs used black canopies with red both-side sashes.

sentences.zh: 其千石、六百石，朱左轓。

translations.literal: Those at one thousand and six hundred piculs had vermillion on the left screen-bar only.
translations.idiomatic: One-thousand- and six-hundred-picul ranks kept red only on the left sash.

sentences.zh: 轓長六尺，下屈廣八寸，上業廣尺二寸，九文，十二初，後謙一寸，若月初生，示不敢自滿也。

translations.literal: The screen-bar was six chi long; the lower bend was eight cun wide; the upper head was one chi two cun wide, nine patterns, twelve notches, the rear modest one cun, like the new moon, showing not daring to be full of oneself.
translations.idiomatic: Each sash was six feet long, eight inches across the lower flare, twelve inches at the crown, cut with nine motifs and twelve scallops, the trailing edge pared back an inch like a crescent moon to signal humility.

sentences.zh: 景帝中元五年，始詔六百石以上施車轓，得銅五末，軛有吉陽筩。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Emperor Jing’s middle era he first ordered that from six hundred piculs upward carriage screen-bars be applied, could use bronze on the five extremities, and the yoke had auspicious tubes.
translations.idiomatic: In Jing’s Zhongyuan 5 an edict allowed six-hundred-picul officials and above to mount carriage sashes, bronze tips on fittings, and lucky tubes on the yoke.

sentences.zh: 中二千石以上右騑，三百石以上皁布蓋，千石以上皁繒覆蓋，二百石以下白布蓋，皆有四維槓衣。

translations.literal: From fully two thousand piculs upward there was a right trace horse; from three hundred piculs upward black cloth canopy; from one thousand piculs upward black silk covering canopy; from two hundred piculs downward white cloth canopy; all had four-cornered tie-ropes and pole cloths.
translations.idiomatic: Two-thousand-picul ranks added a right trace; three hundred and up used black cloth canopies; one thousand and up had black silk overlay; below two hundred, white cloth—all with corner ties and wrapped poles.

sentences.zh: 賈人不得乘馬車。

translations.literal: Merchants were not permitted to ride horse-drawn carriages.
translations.idiomatic: Traders were forbidden horse-drawn passenger carriages.

sentences.zh: 除吏赤畫槓，其餘皆青雲。

translations.literal: Dismissed officials had red-painted pole cloths; the rest all had blue cloud pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Retired officers kept crimson-wrapped shafts; everyone else used blue cloud designs.

sentences.zh: 公、列侯、中二千石、二千石夫人，會朝若蠶，各乘其夫之安車，右騑，加交絡帷裳，皆皁。

translations.literal: Wives of dukes, full marquises, fully two thousand piculs, and two thousand piculs, when attending court or the silkworm rite, each rode her husband’s seated carriage, right trace, with crossed-net curtains and skirt panels, all black.
translations.idiomatic: Wives of dukes, marquises, and two-thousand-picul officials, at court levees or the silkworm ceremony, rode their husbands’ seated cars—right trace, lattice veils, black throughout.

sentences.zh: 非公會，不得乘朝車，得乘漆布輜軿車，銅五末。

translations.literal: If not a public assembly they might not ride the court carriage; they could ride the lacquered cloth covered light carriage with bronze five extremities.
translations.idiomatic: Away from formal assembly they could not use the court car but might take the lacquered cloth gig with bronze-capped fittings.

sentences.zh: 乘輿大駕，公卿奉引，太僕禦，大將軍參乘。

translations.literal: In the great equipage of the palanquin the excellencies led the traces, the grand coachman drove, and the grand general was guard of honor beside the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: For the emperor’s grand progress the three excellencies led the team, the grand coachman held the reins, and the grand general rode escort on the running board.

sentences.zh: 屬車八十一乘，備千乘萬騎。

translations.literal: There were eighty-one attendant chariots, providing for a thousand chariots and ten thousand riders.
translations.idiomatic: The train numbered eighty-one follow-cars, the full complement evoking “thousand chariots, myriad horsemen.”

sentences.zh: 西都行祠天郊，甘泉備之。

translations.literal: When the western capital performed suburban sacrifice to Heaven, Ganquan had the full array.
translations.idiomatic: Western Chang’an staged the suburban rite to Heaven with the full Ganquan equipage.

sentences.zh: 官有其註，名曰甘泉鹵簿。

translations.literal: The office had its annotated roster, called the Ganquan procession book.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry kept an annotated order of march—the “Ganquan procession book.”

sentences.zh: 東都唯大行乃大駕。

translations.literal: In the eastern capital only the grand obsequies used the great equipage.
translations.idiomatic: At Luoyang only the funeral of an emperor deployed the great equipage.

sentences.zh: 大駕，太僕校駕；

translations.literal: In the great equipage the grand coachman inspected the harness;
translations.idiomatic: Under the great-progress order the grand coachman checked every trace and buckle.

sentences.zh: 法駕，黃門令校駕。

translations.literal: Statutory equipage: the Yellow Gate superintendent inspected the harness.
translations.idiomatic: For the middle-grade statutory train the Yellow Gate superintendent checked every strap and buckle.

sentences.zh: 乘輿法駕，公卿不在鹵簿中。

translations.literal: In the statutory equipage of the palanquin the excellencies were not listed in the procession roster.
translations.idiomatic: On a statutory progress the three excellencies did not march inside the formal order of march.

sentences.zh: 河南尹、執金吾、雒陽令奉引，奉車郎禦，侍中參乘。

translations.literal: The governor of Henan, the Bearer of the Golden Mace, and the magistrate of Luoyang led the traces; the Gentleman Attendant of the Carriages drove; an attendant-in-ordinary rode escort on the running board.
translations.idiomatic: The capital intendant, the city’s chief of police, and the Luoyang magistrate led the teams, a carriage gentleman held the reins, and an attendant-in-ordinary took the seat beside the driver.

sentences.zh: 屬車三十六乘。

translations.literal: There were thirty-six attendant chariots.
translations.idiomatic: The follow-train numbered thirty-six cars.

sentences.zh: 前驅有九斿雲罕，鳳皇闟戟，皮軒鸞旗，皆大夫載。

translations.literal: The van had nine-pennon cloud-nets, phoenix halberds with wide crossbars, leather-roofed cars and luan-bird banners—all borne by grandees.
translations.idiomatic: The vanguard displayed nine-streamer cloud-nets, phoenix-patterned ji halberds, leather-canopied scouts, and luan standards, each piece carried by a ranked grandee.

sentences.zh: 鸞旗者，編羽旄，列系幢旁。

translations.literal: The luan banner was plaited feathers and yak-hair tassels, ranged and fastened beside the canopy staff.
translations.idiomatic: The “luan” banner braided pheasant plumes and yak tails along the staff beside the imperial umbrella.

sentences.zh: 民或謂之雞翹，非也。

translations.literal: Commoners sometimes called it a “cock’s crest”; this is incorrect.
translations.idiomatic: Rustics nicknamed it the “chicken plume,” but that name is a vulgar error.

sentences.zh: 後有金鉦黃鉞，黃門鼓車。

translations.literal: Behind came a bronze gong, a yellow ceremonial axe, and the Yellow Gate drum carriage.
translations.idiomatic: The rear brought up a bronze signal gong, a gilded battle-axe, and the eunuch corps’ drum wagon.

sentences.zh: 古者諸侯貳車九乘。

translations.literal: In antiquity feudal lords had nine secondary chariots.
translations.idiomatic: Classical enfeoffed lords were allowed nine escort chariots.

sentences.zh: 秦滅九國，兼其車服，故大駕屬車八十一乘，法駕半之。

translations.literal: Qin extinguished the nine states and annexed their chariots and robes; therefore the great equipage had eighty-one attendant chariots, statutory equipage half that.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin swallowed the rival kingdoms it seized their court trains, which is why the Han “great progress” runs eighty-one follow-cars while the statutory halving uses thirty-six.

sentences.zh: 屬車皆皁蓋赤裡，朱轓，戈矛弩箙，尚書、御史所載。

translations.literal: The attendant chariots all had black canopies with red lining, vermillion screen-bars, and tubes for spears, pikes, and crossbows; they were ridden by secretaries and censors.
translations.idiomatic: Each escort wagon wore a black canopy lined in red, scarlet sashes, and racks for pole-arms and crossbows—manned by masters-of-writing and attending censors.

sentences.zh: 最後一車懸豹尾，豹尾以前比省中。

translations.literal: The last chariot hung a leopard’s tail; everything forward of the leopard tail counted as within the palace secretariat’s zone.
translations.idiomatic: The rearmost car flew a leopard-tail pennant; anyone stationed ahead of that marker was treated as inside the inner-court cordon.

sentences.zh: 行祠天郊以法駕，祠地、明堂省什三，祠宗廟尤省，謂之小駕。

translations.literal: Suburban sacrifice to Heaven used statutory equipage; sacrifice to Earth and the Bright Hall cut the train by three-tenths; sacrifice to the ancestral temples cut still further—this was called light equipage.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven at the southern suburb kept the statutory train; Earth and the Bright Hall shed thirty percent of the escort; temple runs pared the roster again—these were the “light” and “lighter” formations.

sentences.zh: 每出，太僕奉駕上鹵簿，中常侍、小黃門副；

translations.literal: Whenever the ruler went out, the grand coachman presented the carriage and entered it on the procession book; a regular palace attendant and junior yellow gate served as deputies.
translations.idiomatic: On every outing the grand coachman logged the harness and filed the order of march, while a chief eunuch and a junior yellow gate doubled-checked the roster.

sentences.zh: 尚書主者，郎令史副；

translations.literal: The presiding secretary of the Masters’ Bureau, with a clerk-of-gentlemen as deputy;
translations.idiomatic: The duty secretary from the Masters’ Bureau paired with a gentleman’s clerk;

sentences.zh: 侍御史，蘭台令史副。

translations.literal: the attendant censor, with an Orchid Terrace clerk as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: the attending censor paired with an Orchid Terrace archivist.

sentences.zh: 皆執注，以督整車騎，謂之護駕。

translations.literal: All carried annotated slips to supervise and align chariots and riders—this was called guarding the equipage.
translations.idiomatic: Each deputy carried a checked list to line up mounts and carriages—what the court called “escort duty.”

sentences.zh: 春秋上陵，尤省於小駕，直事尚書一人從，其餘令以下，皆先行後罷。

translations.literal: Spring and autumn visits to the imperial tombs were still more reduced than light equipage: one duty secretary of the Masters’ Bureau followed; all others from bureau chief downward went ahead first and were dismissed afterward.
translations.idiomatic: Seasonal tomb pilgrimages used an even slimmer train than the “light” set: only one on-duty secretary rode along, while chiefs of bureau and below cleared the road beforehand and peeled off once the rite ended.

sentences.zh: 輕車，古之戰車也。

translations.literal: The light chariot was the war chariot of antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: The “light car” is the old battlefield chariot, stripped for speed.

sentences.zh: 洞朱輪輿，不巾不蓋，建矛戟幢麾，<輻車>輒弩服。

translations.literal: It had vermillion wheels showing through the body, no leather screen and no canopy; it erected spears, halberds, command banners, and stored crossbow cases and quiver racks on the supply wagon.
translations.idiomatic: Its body showed scarlet through pierced wheels, it carried neither sun-screen nor roof, it bristled with spears, ji, and signal flags, and a trailing supply cart bore bundled crossbows and spare quarrels.

sentences.zh: 藏在武庫。

translations.literal: They were stored in the armory.
translations.idiomatic: The whole detachment lived in the imperial arsenal between parades.

sentences.zh: 大駕、法駕出，射聲校尉、司馬吏士載，以次屬車，在鹵簿中。

translations.literal: When great or statutory equipage went out, the colonel of crossbowmen and marshal officers and men mounted them in order among the attendant chariots within the procession.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the great or statutory train rolled, the colonel of crossbowmen and his staff took these cars in sequence among the follow-wagons inside the cordon.

sentences.zh: 諸車有矛戟，其飾幡斿旗幟皆五采，制度從《周禮》。

translations.literal: The various chariots bore spears and halberds; their pennants, streamers, and flags were all five colors; the regulations followed the Rites of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Each type bristled with pole-arms, while banners and streamers stayed strictly polychrome according to the Zhou canonical scheme.

sentences.zh: 吳、孫《兵法》云：「有巾有蓋，謂之武剛車。

translations.literal: The Wu and Sun Art of War says: “With leather screen and canopy, it is called the armored escort chariot.”
translations.idiomatic: The military treatises of Wu and Sun record: “Add canopy and side screen and you have the armored escort wagon.”

sentences.zh: 」武剛車者，為先驅。

translations.literal: The armored escort chariots served as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Those armored wagons opened the march.

sentences.zh: 又為屬車輕車，為後殿焉。

translations.literal: There were also light chariots among the attendants, serving as rear guard.
translations.idiomatic: Light war cars also brought up the rear of the follow-train.

sentences.zh: 大使車，立乘，駕駟，赤帷。

translations.literal: The great ambassador chariot was ridden standing, harnessed four-in-hand, with red curtains.
translations.idiomatic: Senior envoys used a tall four-horse carriage with crimson hangings, the rider standing to show rank.

sentences.zh: 持節者，重導從：賊曹車、斧車、督車、功曹車皆兩；

translations.literal: Credential bearers had a double escort: burglar-bureau cars, axe cars, supervisor cars, and merit-clerk cars, two of each;
translations.idiomatic: Men carrying the imperial staff drew a heavy escort—paired wagons for the burglar bureau, the display axes, the route supervisor, and the merit clerk;

sentences.zh: 大車，伍伯DA7A弩十二人；

translations.literal: on the large escort wagon twelve foot-runners with crossbows;
translations.idiomatic: the lead baggage wagon added twelve runners with shouldered crossbows;

sentences.zh: 闢車四人；

translations.literal: four road-clearing runners;
translations.idiomatic: four outriders on foot cleared the way;

sentences.zh: 從車四乘。

translations.literal: four follow-cars.
translations.idiomatic: and four light follow-cars trailed behind.

sentences.zh: 無節，單導從，減半。

translations.literal: Without a staff of authority there was a single escort, halved.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys without the bronze staff made do with half that escort and a single file of runners.

sentences.zh: 小使車，不立乘，有騑，赤屏泥油，重絳帷。

translations.literal: The lesser ambassador chariot was not ridden standing; it had a trace horse, red lacquered mudguards, and double crimson curtains.
translations.idiomatic: Junior missions rode seated gigs with a side trace, lacquered red fenders, and doubled scarlet drapes.

sentences.zh: 導無斧車。

translations.literal: The escort lacked the axe display car.
translations.idiomatic: Their vanguard omitted the ceremonial axe wagon.

sentences.zh: 近小使車，蘭輿赤轂，白蓋赤帷。

translations.literal: The “near lesser ambassador” chariot had orchid-pattern sides and red hubs, white canopy and red screens.
translations.idiomatic: Rapid courier gigs used orchid scrollwork on the panels, crimson hubs, a white umbrella roof, and red side screens.

sentences.zh: 從騶騎四十人。

translations.literal: It had forty mounted attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Forty mounted runners rode escort.

sentences.zh: 此謂追捕考案，有所敕取者之所乘也。

translations.literal: This was what those who pursued fugitives, examined cases, or carried imperial writs of seizure rode.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the train for investigators chasing bandits, holding inquests, or serving sealed warrants of arrest.

sentences.zh: 諸使車皆朱班輪，四輻，赤衡軛。

translations.literal: All mission chariots had vermillion-flecked wheels, four spokes, and red yoke and pole.
translations.idiomatic: Every official dispatch vehicle shared speckled red wheels, four-spoke hubs, and scarlet yoke hardware.

sentences.zh: 其送葬，白堊已下，灑車而後還。

translations.literal: For funerals they whitewashed down from the white clay mark, sprinkled the carriages, and then returned.
translations.idiomatic: After obsequies crews whitewashed the lower panels to a set line, sprinkled the wheels for purification, and only then drove the cars back to depot.

sentences.zh: 公、卿、中二千石、二千石，郊廟、明堂、祠陵，法出，皆大車，立乘、駕駟。

translations.literal: Dukes, ministers, fully two thousand piculs, and two thousand piculs, when proceeding by statute to suburban altars, the Bright Hall, or imperial tombs, all used large chariots, standing ride, four-in-hand.
translations.idiomatic: High ministers traveling under statute to suburban shrines, the Bright Hall, or mausolea all stood in heavy four-horse baggage wagons.

sentences.zh: 他出，乘安車。

translations.literal: For other outings they rode seated carriages.
translations.idiomatic: Ordinary business let them drop into enclosed seated carriages.

sentences.zh: 大行載車，其飾如金根車，加施組連璧交絡四角，金龍首銜璧，垂五采，析羽流蘇前後，雲氣畫帷裳，B42E文畫曲轓，長懸車等。

translations.literal: The hearse for grand obsequies was ornamented like the gold-root carriage, with added knotted silks linking jade bi at the four corners, gold dragon heads gripping disks, five-colored pendants, split-feather tassels front and rear, cloud-vapor painted curtains and skirt panels, cloud-beast motifs on the curved screen-bars, long-suspension hearses, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial corpse wagon matched the gold-root state car but layered knotted cords and linked jade discs at each corner, gilt dragon jaws clutching ritual bi, polychrome silk tassels, plume fringes fore and aft, painted cloud veils, curved sashes with beast scrollwork, and the extended “long suspension” hearse style.

sentences.zh: 太僕禦，駕六布施馬。

translations.literal: The grand coachman drove; it was harnessed six-in-hand with “alms-distribution” horses.
translations.idiomatic: The grand coachman handled six horses—the special white team reserved for the funeral train.

sentences.zh: 布施馬者，淳白駱馬也，以黑藥灼其身為虎文。

translations.literal: “Alms-distribution horses” means pure white piebald horses whose bodies were branded with tiger stripes in black medicine.
translations.idiomatic: Those “distribution” mounts were snowy piebalds whose hides were singed with black paste into tiger stripes for the catafalque team.

sentences.zh: 既下，馬斥賣，車藏城北秘宮，皆不得入城門。

translations.literal: After the interment the horses were sold off, the chariots were stored in the secret palace north of the wall, and none were permitted through the city gates.
translations.idiomatic: Once the mound was closed the horses went to public auction, the hearses were locked in the northern vault outside the walls, and neither team nor car might re-enter the capital gates.

sentences.zh: 當用，太僕考工乃內飾治，禮吉凶不相干也。

translations.literal: When they were to be used again, the grand coachman and the Directorate of Works refitted the interiors—auspicious and inauspicious rites did not interfere with each other.
translations.idiomatic: Before another use the grand coachman and the Works office refitted the interiors so mourning gear never mingled with living court ritual.

sentences.zh: 公卿以下至縣三百石長導從，置門下五吏：賊曹、督盜賊、功曹，皆帶劍，三車導；

translations.literal: From excellencies downward to county chiefs of three hundred piculs there was an escort, with five gate clerks—burglar bureau, bandit supervisor, merit clerk—all bearing swords, three cars leading;
translations.idiomatic: Everyone from the three excellencies down to a three-hundred-picul county chief traveled with five household runners—burglar clerk, thief-catcher, merit clerk—each sword-armed, and three lead cars;

sentences.zh: 主簿、主記，兩車為從。

translations.literal: the registrar and recorder had two cars as followers.
translations.idiomatic: the chief registrar and chief recorder each rated a follow-wagon.

sentences.zh: 縣令以上，加導斧車。

translations.literal: From county magistrate upward they added a leading axe display car.
translations.idiomatic: County magistrates and above added the axe-bearing vanguard wagon.

sentences.zh: 公乘安車，則前後並馬立乘。

translations.literal: When a duke rode the seated carriage, front and rear horses stood paired for a standing ride.
translations.idiomatic: A duke in a covered carriage still posted outriders fore and aft as if standing in a state car.

sentences.zh: 長安、雒陽令及王國都縣加前後兵車，亭長，設右騑，駕兩。

translations.literal: The magistrates of Chang’an and Luoyang and the metropolitan counties of princely kingdoms added front and rear military cars, ward heads, a right trace, and two-horse harness.
translations.idiomatic: Chang’an’s and Luoyang’s magistrates, plus capital county chiefs in kingdoms, doubled the escort with armored vans fore and aft, ward captains, a right-side trace horse, and two-horse teams.

sentences.zh: 弩車前伍伯，公八人，中二千石、二千石、六百石皆四人，自四百石以下至二百石皆二人。

translations.literal: Before the crossbow cart the foot-runners: for a duke eight men; for fully two thousand piculs, two thousand piculs, and six hundred piculs, four each; from four hundred piculs down to two hundred piculs, two each.
translations.idiomatic: Foot runners marching ahead of the crossbow wagon numbered eight for a duke, four for top ministers and six-hundred-picul ranks, and two for everyone from four hundred down to two hundred piculs.

sentences.zh: 黃綬，武官伍伯，文官闢車。

translations.literal: Yellow-ribbon officials: military officers used foot-runners; civil officials used clearing cars.
translations.idiomatic: Officials with the yellow ribbon gave military posts foot escorts and civil posts light clearing carriages.

sentences.zh: 鈴下、侍閣、門蘭、部署、街里走卒，皆有程品，多少隨所典領。

translations.literal: Bell attendants, chamber ushers, gate guards, office runners, and ward foot soldiers all had graded quotas; their numbers followed the office held.
translations.idiomatic: Grooms, doorkeepers, gate sergeants, clerical runners, and neighborhood constables each drew fixed complements scaled to the magistrate’s jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 驛馬三十里一置，卒皆赤幘絳云。

translations.literal: Relay horses were posted every thirty li; the runners all wore red turbans and crimson.
translations.idiomatic: Post stations sat thirty li apart on the highways, every courier in a scarlet kerchief and crimson coat.

sentences.zh: 古者軍出，師旅皆從；

translations.literal: In antiquity when armies marched, hosts and brigades all followed;
translations.idiomatic: Ancient hosts on campaign marched with full brigades in train;

sentences.zh: 秦省其卒，取其師旅之名焉。

translations.literal: Qin eliminated the foot soldiers but took the names of hosts and brigades.
translations.idiomatic: Qin cut the infantry tail but kept the old names “army” and “brigade” for its escort labels.

sentences.zh: 公以下至二千石，騎吏四人，千石以下至三百石，縣長二人，皆帶劍，持戟為前列，揵弓<韋蜀>九鞬。

translations.literal: From dukes down to two thousand piculs there were four mounted clerks; from one thousand piculs down to three hundred piculs, county chiefs had two; all wore swords, held halberds in the front rank, and slung bows with nine quivers.
translations.idiomatic: Dukes through two-thousand-picul ministers rated four mounted attendants; magistrates from one thousand down to three hundred piculs had two; every man went armed with sword, halberd at the van, bow on the back, and nine-tube quiver.

sentences.zh: 諸侯王法駕，官屬傅相以下，皆備鹵簿，似京都官騎，張弓帶鞬，遮迾出入稱促。

translations.literal: For princely kings in statutory equipage, from tutors and chancellors downward, all had full processions like capital officials on horseback, bows strung and quivers hung, screening comings and goings with tight cordons.
translations.idiomatic: A king’s statutory progress duplicated the capital model: from chancellor down every aide rode in the roster with strung bows, filled quivers, and tight pickets controlling every crossing.

sentences.zh: 列侯，家丞、庶子導從。

translations.literal: Full marquises were escorted by household aide and junior steward.
translations.idiomatic: Marquises made do with their household steward and junior son-of-the-house leading the escort.

sentences.zh: 若會耕祠，主縣假給闢車鮮明卒，備其威儀。

translations.literal: If they joined the ploughing or sacrifice, the host county lent clearing cars and bright runners to complete the display.
translations.idiomatic: For the spring plough or joint sacrifices the county seat loaned road-clearing wagons and liveried runners to fill out the spectacle.

sentences.zh: 導從事畢，皆罷所假。

translations.literal: When the escort duty was finished, all borrowed items were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Once the rite ended every borrowed runner and vehicle went back to county stock.

sentences.zh: 諸車之文：乘輿，倚龍伏虎，文畫輈，龍首鸞衡，重牙班輪，昇龍飛軨。

translations.literal: Patterns on the various chariots: the palanquin had leaning dragon and crouching tiger, patterned painting on the shaft, dragon head and luan on the crossbeam, double-toothed speckled wheels, ascending dragon and flying nave-bosses.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial cars showed paired dragons and tigers on the panels, painted beasts along the pole, dragon and luan on the yoke, double-notched red wheels, and flying hub caps figured with ascending dragons.

sentences.zh: 皇太子、諸侯王，倚虎伏鹿，文畫輈轓，吉陽，朱班輪，鹿文飛軨，旂旗九降龍。

translations.literal: Heir apparent and princely kings had leaning tiger and crouching deer, patterned painting on shaft and screen-bars, auspicious tubes, vermillion-flecked wheels, deer-pattern flying nave-bosses, and banners with nine descending dragons.
translations.idiomatic: Heirs and kings swapped the dragon for tiger-and-deer pairs, kept lucky tubes and speckled wheels, carved deer motifs on the hubs, and flew nine-dragon ensigns.

sentences.zh: 公、列侯，倚鹿伏熊，黑轓，朱班輪，鹿文飛軨，九降龍。

translations.literal: Dukes and full marquises had leaning deer and crouching bear, black screen-bars, vermillion-flecked wheels, deer-pattern flying nave-bosses, and nine descending dragons.
translations.idiomatic: Dukes and marquises paired deer and bear, blackened their sashes, and still flew the nine-dragon pattern on lesser banners.

sentences.zh: 卿，朱兩轓，五降龍。

translations.literal: Ministers had vermillion on both screen-bars and five descending dragons.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers of state doubled the red sashes and dropped to five dragons on the staff.

sentences.zh: 二千石以下各從科品，諸轓車以上，軛皆有吉陽。

translations.literal: From two thousand piculs downward each followed his grade; for all covered gigs and above, the yoke always bore auspicious tubes.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone below two thousand piculs matched ornament to salary rank, but any covered gig upward still mounted the bronze “lucky” tubes on the yoke.

sentences.zh: 諸馬之文：案乘輿，金方釳，插翟象鑣，龙画𦁕，沫昇龍，赤扇汗，青兩翅，燕尾。

translations.literal: Patterns on the various horses: for the palanquin, gold nave-cap, inserted pheasant plumes and ivory cheek-pieces, dragon painting on the forehead strap, froth pattern of ascending dragon, red sweat cloth, blue twin wings, swallow tail.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial teams wore gold hub caps, pheasant plumes, ivory bits, dragon scrolls on the brow band, foam-white ascending dragons on the cheek pieces, crimson chest cloths, blue “double wings,” and swallow-tail cruppers.

sentences.zh: 駙馬，左右赤珥流蘇，飛鳥節，赤膺兼。

translations.literal: The trace horses had left and right red pendant tassels, flying-bird bosses, and red breast bands mixed together.
translations.idiomatic: Outriders flanked the team with crimson ear tassels, bird-shaped cheek bosses, and doubled scarlet breast bands.

sentences.zh: 皇太子或亦如之。

translations.literal: The heir apparent sometimes was the same.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince’s outriders often matched this harness scheme.

sentences.zh: 王、公、列侯，鏤鍚文髦，朱鑣朱鹿，朱文，絳扇汗，青翅燕尾。

translations.literal: Kings, dukes, and full marquises had openwork tin bosses, patterned manes, vermillion cheek-pieces and vermillion deer, vermillion patterns, crimson sweat cloths, blue wings and swallow tail.
translations.idiomatic: Kings, dukes, and marquises used pierced tin bosses, figured manes, scarlet bits and deer motifs, red brocade on the breast, blue side wings, and swallow-tail cruppers.

sentences.zh: 卿以下有騑者，緹扇汗，青翅尾，當盧文髦，上下皆通。

translations.literal: Ministers downward who had trace horses used yellow-brown sweat cloths, blue wings and tail, patterned manes on the forehead boss, and the same above and below throughout.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers with side traces shifted to tawny chest cloths, blue wings and tail tassels, and patterned brow bosses on both lead and trace mounts.

sentences.zh: 中二千石以上及使者，乃有騑駕云。

translations.literal: Only from fully two thousand piculs upward and for envoys were there trace-drawn carriages.
translations.idiomatic: Only officials at “full two thousand piculs” and credentialed envoys rated the paired trace horses described above.
